note: Hand-maintained list of northern high-water events that are not in NRCan Historical Flood Events. Add rows with a source link for each.

properties.summary: Lac La Ronge rose to a record high, the record that stood until 2020, with record flows on the Montreal River. Flooded roads forced evacuations at Montreal Lake Cree Nation and Timber Bay.

sources.title: MBC Radio, 2011: Montreal Lake partially evacuates due to flooding
National Observer, August 20, 2020: Threat from record-breaking water levels starts to let up

properties.summary: Buffalo Narrows received 111.8 mm of rain in one day, most of it within 12 hours, which the Water Security Agency called more than a 1-in-100-year event. Water rose up to homes and swamped Buffalo Narrows park, and the agency warned of rising flows on the Churchill River upstream of Patuanak.

sources.title: CBC News, July 2017: Buffalo Narrows rainfall
Canadian Underwriter (Canadian Press), July 26, 2017: Northern Saskatchewan village hit with buckets of water from record rain
Global News, July 2017: Buffalo Narrows region dealing with 1-in-100-year rainfall

properties.summary: A very wet June and July pushed northern lakes and rivers to record highs. Lac La Ronge peaked above its 2011 record, and on July 29 the Water Security Agency reclassified the La Ronge Dam, upstream of Stanley Mission, as a potential dam failure and sandbagged it. The Churchill River near Sandy Bay crested above its 2005 record in early August.

sources.title: National Observer, July 29, 2020: More flooding on top of flooding, potential failure of northeast Saskatchewan dam
National Observer, August 20, 2020: Threat from record-breaking water levels starts to let up
larongeNOW, July 31, 2020: Reindeer River, Churchill River near Sandy Bay exceed historical highs
Water Security Agency: Northern Saskatchewan Summer High Water Update, August 28, 2020

properties.summary: High flows on the Beaver River peaked near Beauval in early July. Lac Île-à-la-Crosse peaked at about 421.1 m around July 28, and the village sandbagged and built berms. The Water Security Agency expected levels to stay above normal into the winter.

sources.title: paNOW, July 9, 2020: River expected to rise by 40 to 50 cm Friday
meadowlakeNOW, July 22, 2020: Northern mayors believe permanent berms needed as water rises
Water Security Agency: Northern Saskatchewan Summer High Water Update, July 24, 2020
